title: quarterly-sync-ops-playbook-v0-1
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is the working plan for synchronizing company-level objectives (draft OKRs), the executive update narrative, and the all-team sync (company-wide meeting) for the coming quarter. Aim is to produce a single coherent message that aligns engineering, product, GTM, and support around measurable priorities and clear owner commitments.

Context / constraints:
- Market: competitor open-model pushes + new infra options mean we must emphasize serving economics and reliability in public comms.
- Timing: all-team sync targeted for first week of Q2 (week of Apr 6). Final OKRs must be frozen two weeks before sync for slide production.
- Audience: engineers (runtime + infra), product leads, sales/CS, customers. Keep technical tradeoffs visible for engineering audience; keep customer impact metrics prominent for GTM.

Topline draft company objectives (working):
1) Objective: Make inference predictable for customers at scale
   - KR1: Achieve 95th percentile token latency < 120ms for hosted-api 2k token tail across top-10 models
   - KR2: Deploy dedicated autoscaling that maintains <2% request throttling under 2x baseline traffic in prod
   - KR3: Publish public performance profiles for 12 curated models with reproducible benchmark scripts

2) Objective: Improve cost-efficiency while preserving output quality
   - KR1: Reduce average per-token serving cost (hosted) by 30% vs baseline by optimizing batching and KV caching
   - KR2: Ship quantization-and-recommendation tool in Redwood Optimize MVP and onboard 3 internal customers
   - KR3: Achieve 10% reduction in customer invoice disputes related to metering by clarifying token semantics in docs

3) Objective: Enterprise readiness and trust
   - KR1: Complete SOC2 type II readiness checklist items prioritized for Private deployments (90% complete)
   - KR2: Launch private-deploy VPC GA in 2 regions with KMS integration and audit log ingestion
   - KR3: Reduce enterprise onboarding time (first inference call to production) from 6 weeks to 3 weeks for Dedicated customers

Notes on scope: these are company-level drafts. Each product line (hosted, dedicated, private, optimize, console) should map 1:1 to at least one KR. Expect engineering owners to decompose into execution milestones by Mar 20.

Executive update draft (CEO / Headline bullets):
- Quick wins: published perf profiles for 5 models, closed loop on two major customer regressions, Dedicated pilot capacity doubled for two tier-1 customers.
- Strategic priority: shift investment toward serving runtime efficiency + routing policies to protect SLAs while lowering unit costs.
- Ask from teams: finalize product-level success metrics by Mar 18; readiness gate for GA launches is a passing end-to-end cost/latency regression test.

All-team sync (high level agenda, 60–75 minutes):
- 00:00–00:05 Welcome + theme (CEO) — framing: "Serving is our moat"
- 00:05–00:15 Company KPIs snapshot (CFO/Head of Growth) — revenue, gross margin on hosting, NRR signals, paying customers trending
- 00:15–00:30 Product priorities (VP Product) — top 3 launches, demo of Optimize recommendation flow (30s clip)
- 00:30–00:45 Engineering deep-dive (CTO/Head of Serving Runtime) — latency improvements, rollout plan for autoscaled Dedicated pools, SLOs and degradation behavior
- 00:45–00:55 Customer stories & support highlights (Head CS) — one case study and churn prevention wins
- 00:55–01:05 Live Q&A (moderated) — collect unknowns and follow-ups
- 01:05–01:15 Close & next steps (CEO) — commit to published OKRs and follow-up small-group town halls

Communications plan / channels:
- Pre-read (to be sent Apr 1): 1-pager + slide core deck (master slide due Mar 20).
- Internal sync: company announcement in #company-announce + pinned Confluence doc with OKR mapping and owners.
- External comms: blog post outline (marketing) to emphasize performance & cost wins scheduled April 2 post-sync.
- Follow-up: small-group breakouts by function week after sync to translate company-OKRs into team plans.

Deliverables + deadlines (owners):
- Final company OKRs (Mar 15) — Owner: Marisa Chen
- Exec slide deck draft (Mar 20) — Owner: Jordan Lee (product comms), input from Diego on infra metrics
- Performance benchmark artifacts (Mar 18) — Owner: Head of Serving Runtime (Diego Ramirez)
- Customer case study draft (Mar 22) — Owner: Samira Gupta (CS)
- Pre-read distribution (Apr 1) — Owner: Head of Comms (Aisha Kapoor)

Meeting logistics / ops checklist (quick):
- Book large room + Livestream (AV) — ops to confirm by Mar 25
- MC + Q&A moderator assigned — Jordan Lee accepted; backup: Aisha Kapoor
- Captioning + live transcript enabled — accessibility lead to confirm
- Recording and slides upload to shared drive immediately post event

Risks & open questions (explicit):
- Risk: finalizing model perf numbers could move the narrative if any metric regresses. Mitigation: include "data freshness" footnote and show trends not single numbers.
- Question: do we publicly commit to per-token-cost reductions? Legal/finance sign-off needed; target decision Mar 12.
- Risk: cross-team alignment on Dedicated autoscale policy; mitigation: two technical town halls (eng + infra) before sync.

Pre-reads and prep for team leads:
- Engineering leads: bring a 2-slide summary (progress vs KR, 3 blockers) by Mar 16.
- Product: one slide per product area with launch readiness and risk matrix by Mar 18.
- GTM: customer impact slide and 2 top customer quotes by Mar 20.
- CS/Sales: a short one-pager on enterprise onboarding improvements by Mar 18.

Action items (initial):
- [Marisa] circulate this playbook and request decomposition templates by Mar 3.
- [Jordan] own slide deck template + coordinate rehearsals (dates: Mar 26 & Apr 2).
- [Diego] produce benchmark artifacts and reproducible scripts by Mar 18; include runbook for replication.
- [Aisha] draft external blog outline and get legal review by Mar 12.
- [Samira] draft customer case study and secure permissions by Mar 22.

Notes to self / working reminders (informal):
- Keep language simple: engineers want details but company message should center on customer outcomes.
- Expect last-minute perf changes; maintain slide versioning (v1/v2/vFINAL) and date-stamped assets.
- Slack thread: start #q2-sync-ops today for asynchronous clarifications — pin this doc.

Appendix: suggested talking points for execs (bullet bank)
- "We treat serving as a first-class product. Customers pay for predictable latency and controlled cost — that informs our roadmap."
- "Our short-term investments reduce unit cost while preserving quality; long-term we position for multi-cloud private deployments."
- "We will publish reproducible profiles so customers can choose tradeoffs with confidence."

End of draft.

Open: feedback due Mar 12 so owners can update deliverables and freeze OKRs on Mar 15.

----
Version notes: v0-1 working draft; expect multiple edits. This doc intentionally mixes polished asks (deliverables) and working notes for owners.
